safi-cedvel:15-15.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is circumstantial (ḥāl) — or resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya) — (لا) is negating, and the fāʿil (agent) of (يخاف) is a pronoun referring to the agent of سوّاها, i.e. Allah [Note: It is possible that it refers to the warning Messenger, or to the one who hamstrung the she-camel.].
Clause: «لا يخاف ... » is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from the agent of سوّاها [Note: It is possible that it is resumptive, with no grammatical position.].

* Morphology:
(يخاف): it contains an ʿilāl (weak-letter change) by substitution; its origin is يخوف — with fatḥa on the wāw — its maṣdar (verbal noun) is الخوف. The vowel of the wāw was transferred to the khāʾ, then the wāw was changed to alif because the preceding letter has fatḥa.
(عقباها): a noun meaning the consequence of a matter, or its outcome; its pattern is فعلى, with ḍamma on the first letter and sukūn on the second.

* Rhetoric:
Representative metaphor (isti'āra tamthīliyya): in His saying, the Exalted, «وَلا يَخافُ عُقْباها».
That is, its outcome and its consequence, just as punishing kings fear the outcome and consequence of what they do. It is a representative metaphor, expressing their humiliation and that they are abased before Allah, Majestic is His Majesty.

safi-cedvel:1-8.t:
* I'rab:
(والشمس) is attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "I swear" (أقسم). (إذا) is an adverb stripped of the conditional sense, in the position of accusative, attached to the implied verb أقسم, and likewise in the next two places. (ما) is a maṣdar particle «[Note: if it is permissible to use (ما) for rational beings or for individuals of those with knowledge, it is a relative noun in the position of genitive conjoined to السماء, and likewise in the next two places]» in the three places. (الفاء) is a conjunction ...
And the interpreted maṣdar (ما بناها..) is in the position of genitive, conjoined to السماء.
And the interpreted maṣdar (ما طحاها..) is in the position of genitive, conjoined to الأرض.
And the interpreted maṣdar (ما سوّاها) is in the position of genitive, conjoined to نفس.
Clause: « (أقسم) بالشمس ... » has no grammatical position (inceptive).
And the clause: «تلاها ... » is in the position of genitive as a muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause: «جلّاها ... » is in the position of genitive as a muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause: «يغشاها ... » is in the position of genitive as a muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause: «بناها ... » has no grammatical position (ṣila of the particle-like relative (ما), the first).
And the clause: «طحاها ... » has no grammatical position (ṣila of the particle-like relative (ما), the second).
And the clause: «سوّاها ... » has no grammatical position (ṣila of the particle-like relative (ما), the third).
And the clause: «ألهمها ... » has no grammatical position (conjoined to the clause سوّاها) ... The answer to the oath is omitted, its implied form being "You will surely be raised" «[Note: or "Allah will surely destroy the disbelievers of Mecca" — as in al-Kashshāf — and it may be that the answer to the oath is the clause قد أفلح ... — in verse (9) of this sūra — with the lām omitted because of the length of the speech]».

* Morphology:
(2) تلاها: it contains a weakening by substitution; the original is تلوها — its imperfect is يتلو, with fatḥa on the wāw — and when the wāw was vowelled after a fatḥa it was changed into alif.
(3) جلّاها: it contains a weakening by substitution; the original is جلّيها — with the yāʾ vowelled with fatḥa — and the yāʾ was changed into alif because it was vowelled after a fatḥa.
(6) طحاها: i.e. "He spread it out". It contains a weakening by substitution; it is said that the original is طحوها, and it is said طحيها. In al-Qāmūs: طحا like سعى means "to spread out"; and طحا يطحو means "to be far away", "to perish", and "to throw a person on his face"; and الطحا is the flat part of the earth.
(8) فجور: a samāʿī maṣdar of the triliteral فجر; its wazn is فعول (with ḍamma on the fāʾ and the ʿayn).

safi-cedvel:9-10.t:
* I'rab:
(قد) is a particle of confirmation in both places. (من) is a relative noun in the position of accusative as a direct object in both places ..
Clause: «قد أفلح من ... » has no grammatical position (explanatory resumptive) «[Note: or it is the answer to the oath, with the lām omitted because of the length of the speech]».
And the clause: «زكّاها ... » has no grammatical position (ṣila (relative clause) of the first relative noun (من)).
And the clause: «قد خاب من ... » has no grammatical position (conjoined to the resumptive clause).
And the clause: «دسّاها ... » has no grammatical position (ṣila of the second relative noun (من)).

* Morphology:
(9) زكّاها: it contains a weakening by substitution; the ʿayn of the verb in its bare form is a wāw, which was vowelled after a fatḥa and was changed into alif.
(10) خاب: it contains a weakening by substitution; the original is خيب — its imperfect is يخيب — the yāʾ was vowelled after a fatḥa and was changed into alif.
(دسّاها) it is said that the alif is converted from a sīn and the original is دسّسها — with three sīns — and when similar letters followed one another, the sīn was changed into yāʾ, then a weakening by substitution took place in it. The lexicographers said: the original is دسّسها from التدسيس, which is hiding a thing within a thing, so its sīn was replaced by a yāʾ.

safi-cedvel:11-14.t:
* I'rab:
(بطغواها) is attached to (كذّبت), and the (باء) is of causality, or of figurative instrumentality. (إذ) is an adverb in the position of accusative, attached to (كذّبت). (الفاء) is a conjunction. (لهم) is attached to (قال). (ناقة) is a direct object of an omitted verb in the manner of warning (taḥdhīr), i.e. "leave the she-camel of Allah", i.e. "beware of hamstringing her". (سقياها) is conjoined to ناقة, accusative.
Clause: «كذّبت ثمود» has no grammatical position (resumptive).
And the clause: «انبعث أشقاها» is in the position of genitive as a muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause: «قال لهم رسول ... » has no grammatical position (conjoined to the resumptive clause).
And the clause: « (ذروا) ناقة الله ... » is in the position of accusative as the quoted speech (maqūl al-qawl).
Verse 14: (الفاء) is a conjunction in the four places. (عليهم) is attached to (دمدم), meaning "He covered over". (بذنبهم) is attached to (دمدم), and the (باء) is of causality.
And the clause: «كذّبوه ... » has no grammatical position (conjoined to the clause قال لهم).
And the clause: «عقروها ... » has no grammatical position (conjoined to the clause كذّبوه).
And the clause: «دمدم عليهم ربّهم ... » has no grammatical position (conjoined to the clause عقروها).
And the clause: «سوّاها ... » has no grammatical position (conjoined to the clause دمدم).

* Morphology:
(11) طغواها: a samāʿī maṣdar of the triliteral طغا يطغو (the pattern of نصر) and طغى يطغى (the pattern of فتح); its wazn is فعلى.
(13) سقياها: the noun from السقي, or what is used to give drink; its wazn is فعلى (with ḍamma and sukūn). The alif in (السقيا) is written long because a yāʾ precedes it.

* Benefits:
- Incitement (ighrāʾ) and warning (taḥdhīr):
1- Taḥdhīr is a manner of speech by which the addressee is alerted to a disliked matter so that he avoids it.
2- Ighrāʾ is a manner of speech by which the addressee is encouraged to a praiseworthy matter so that he undertakes it.
3- The two manners, taḥdhīr and ighrāʾ, share the following forms:
(a) That the thing warned against and the thing incited to is mentioned as a single word, accusative by an omitted verb, permissibly, such as:
(الكذب فإنه طريق الشر) i.e. "beware of lying", (الصدق فإنه طريق البرّ) i.e. "keep to truthfulness". Here omission of the verb is permissible, that is, mentioning it is not wrong.
(b) That each of them occurs repeated, such as (الكذب الكذب فإنه طريق الفجور), (الصدق الصدق فإنه طريق البر).
(c) That each of them occurs with a conjoined noun, such as (الأمانة والإحسان فإنهما من خلق المؤمن) (الكذب والغشّ فإنهما طريق الهلاك). In the last two cases (b, c) omission of the verb is obligatory. We parse the noun as accusative by ighrāʾ and taḥdhīr; if it is repeated, we parse the repeated one as a verbal emphasis (tawkīd lafẓī) with no grammatical position, while the conjoined one is a noun conjoined to the one incited to or warned against.
Taḥdhīr alone has one form, namely its being introduced by the accusative pronoun (إيّاك) and its derivatives: إياكما- إياكم- إياكن- ... etc.), after which comes the thing warned against, conjoined to it or put in the genitive with من, such as: (إياك والكذب) or (إياك من الكذب). We parse إياك: in the position of accusative by taḥdhīr, and الكذب: the wāw is a conjunction; الكذب is a direct object of an omitted verb, its implied form being "avoid", i.e. ("beware, you, and avoid lying").
